_source: Each state's (and D.C.'s) own election authority: the voter lookup it publishes on its own domain, or a vendor portal it links as its official tool. Never a third-party aggregator. National fallback: USAGov's state election office directory (https://www.usa.gov/election-office).
_method: Per state, the page where a voter sees their sample ballot or polling place: the state's personal lookup when an automated check can reach it, else the authority's own polling-place page that links it. Each was opened through the pipeline's HTTP client with BROWSER_HEADERS (what refresh_link_verification sends) from the development workstation and from production, and `_checked` records what was found. A state whose lookup sits behind a bot wall keeps its official URL, marked UNVERIFIABLE, and is never worked around (AGENTS.md section 7): the link check cannot confirm it, so its page shows the national directory until the wall stops refusing the check.
_note: A dead link on 'here is how to see your real ballot', during election week, from a link Civitas vouched for, is the worst failure this feature has. So per-state URLs are gated: an entry is rendered only once `verified_at` is set by the liveness check (app/pipeline/fetch/ballot_lookup.py), which this file never sets. The check reads its candidate URLs from this file every run, so an edit here reaches the site on the next election run. Unverified or missing entries fall back to the national directory, which is stable and maintained by USAGov.
